p.scope-of-this-document: **Scope of this document.** This file is the maintainer's operating guide: the *shape of a normal day* (commit on mainline, fan out at natural checkpoints), *handling reported drift* (investigate, reconcile into mainline, re-fan — never clobber), *onboarding a host*, and *offboarding a host*.

p.sibling-document-pointers: The model behind it is in [`SOURCE-MIRRORS-PROTOCOL.xml`](SOURCE-MIRRORS-PROTOCOL.xml); the machinery in [`fanout-mechanics.xml`](fanout-mechanics.xml).

quote.THE-LOOP-IN-ONE-LINE: A change arrives somewhere → you review and accept it there → you bring it into local `main` → you fan out → it is everywhere.

p.everything-below-is-that-sentence-expand: Everything below is that sentence, expanded.

normal-day.title: A normal day

p.YOU-WORK-ON-MAINLINE-THE-WAY-YOU-ALWAYS-: You work on mainline the way you always have.

p.COMMIT-LOCALLY-IN-ATOMIC-COMMITS: Commit locally, in atomic commits, with well-formed messages.

p.MULTI-HOMING-DOES-NOT-CHANGE-HOW-YOU-AUT: Nothing about being multi-homed changes how you *author* history.

p.FAN-OUT-AT-NATURAL-CHECKPOINTS: What is new is one habit: **fan out at natural checkpoints.**

p.not-after-every-commit: Not after every commit — after a coherent unit of work, the same moments you would have pushed in a single-host project:

td.ROW-MOMENT-END-OF-A-WORK-SESSION-ACTION: Fan out as the wind-down step

td.ROW-MOMENT-BEFORE-STEPPING-AWAY: Before stepping away for a while

normal-day.fence: # ... a session's worth of commits on mainline ... project-mirror --check # optional: confirm where the hosts stand project-mirror # push main + tags to every host, ff-only

p.THE-FAN-OUT-IS-A-DELIBERATE-ACT-NOT-A-DA: The fan-out is a **deliberate act, not a daemon.**

p.NO-BACKGROUND-JOB-RACES-YOUR-COMMITS-TO-: There is no background job racing your commits to the hosts; you decide when the world sees the new history.

p.THAT-IS-WHAT-KEEPS-MAINLINE-THE-SINGLE-W: That is what keeps mainline the single writer — nothing pushes but you, when you say so.

integrate.title: Integrating an accepted change

p.a-contribution-reaches-mainline-one-of-t: A contribution reaches mainline one of two ways, depending on where you accepted it:

facts.ROUTE-YOU-MERGED-IT-VIA-A-HOSTS-WEB-UI: **You merged it via a host's web UI.** That host's `main` is now ahead. Bring it home *before* fanning out:

integrate.fence: git fetch <that-host-url> main git merge --ff-only FETCH_HEAD project-mirror

facts.ROUTE-YOU-INTEGRATE-LOCALLY: **You integrate locally** — a fork branch, or an emailed patch. On `main` with a clean tree:

integrate.fence: git fetch <contributor-url> <their-branch> # or: git am < patch.eml git merge --ff-only FETCH_HEAD # or your chosen merge project-mirror

p.EITHER-WAY-THE-CHANGE-LANDS-IN-MAINLINE-: Either way, the shape is identical: the change lands in **mainline first**, and only the fan-out puts it on the hosts.

p.A-WEB-UI-MERGE-BUTTON-IS-AN-INBOX-EVENT: A web-UI "Merge" button is an *inbox event*, not integration.

drift.title: Handling reported drift

p.DRIFT-MEANS-THE-HOST-CARRIES-A-MAIN-YOU-: `--check` (or a host warning) reports **DRIFT** on a host: it carries a `main` your mainline does not.

p.drift-is-almost-always-a-direct-write-or: Almost always this is a direct write or a force-push to that host — exactly the thing the model forbids, surfaced loud instead of silently reconciled.

p.DO-NOT-RE-RUN-THE-FAN-OUT-HOPING-IT-CLEA: Do **not** re-run the fan-out hoping it clears.

p.THE-FAN-OUT-REFUSES-TO-FORCE-BY-DESIGN: It will not — the fan-out refuses to force, by design.

facts.DRIFT-STEP-INVESTIGATE: **Investigate.** Fetch the host and look at what it has that you do not.

drift.fence: git fetch <host-url> main git log --oneline main..FETCH_HEAD # the host's extra commits

facts.DRIFT-STEP-DECIDE: **Decide.** Are those commits wanted? Usually someone pushed a real fix directly. Sometimes it is junk to discard.
facts.DRIFT-STEP-RECONCILE-INTO-MAINLINE: **Reconcile *into* mainline.** Merge or cherry-pick the wanted commits onto mainline. Now mainline is ahead of the host again.

drift.fence: git merge FETCH_HEAD # or cherry-pick the good ones

facts.DRIFT-STEP-RE-FAN: **Re-fan.** `project-mirror` — the host fast-forwards cleanly, because mainline now contains its history.

quote.A-DIVERGED-TARGET-IS-A-SIGNAL-TO-INVESTI: A diverged target is a signal to investigate, never something to silently clobber.

p.NEVER-FIX-DRIFT-BY-OVERWRITING-THE-HOST: The one thing you never do is "fix" drift by overwriting the host to match mainline.

p.overwriting-discards-the-work-that-cause: That discards whatever real work caused the drift — which is precisely the data the loud failure was protecting.

p.adding-a-host-is-deliberately-small: Adding a host is deliberately small:

facts.ONBOARD-STEP-CREATE-AN-EMPTY-REPO: **Create an empty repo** on the new host (no README, no initial commit — it must be empty so the first fan-out is a clean fast-forward from nothing).
facts.ONBOARD-STEP-ADD-ONE-MANIFEST-ENTRY: **Add one manifest entry** — name, url, mode, refs — and commit it. The commit is the audit trail for "when did this host join".

facts.ONBOARD-STEP-ENSURE-ACCESS: **Ensure access** — your key can push to it (`push` mode), or the host is configured to mirror itself (`self-pull` mode).
facts.ONBOARD-STEP-FIRST-FAN-OUT: **First fan-out.** `project-mirror`. The new host receives the full history; every existing host is a no-op.

p.the-model-was-built-for-a-living-host-se: No re-architecture, no cutover — the model was built for the host set to be *living*.

p.removing-a-host-is-smaller-still: Removing a host is smaller still:

facts.OFFBOARD-STEP-DELETE-ITS-TARGET-ENTRY: **Delete its `[[target]]` entry** from the manifest and commit the removal. The fan-out stops targeting it immediately.
facts.OFFBOARD-STEP-OPTIONALLY-ARCHIVE-THE-HOS: **Optionally archive the host copy** — leave it read-only as a historical mirror, or delete the repo on that host.

p.NOTHING-IS-LOST-EITHER-WAY: Nothing is lost either way: **every remaining host holds the full history of the declared refs, and mainline holds the whole tree.**

p.OFFBOARDING-NEVER-SUBTRACTS-A-COMMIT: Offboarding a mirror never subtracts a commit from the project — it only stops one replica from being kept current.

p.the-host-set-can-shrink-as-freely-as-it-: That is the payoff of "every host is a complete replica": the host set can shrink as freely as it grew.

facts.SUM-AUTHOR-ON-MAINLINE-AND-FAN-OUT-AT-CH: Author on mainline as normal; fan out at natural checkpoints, never as a background daemon.
facts.SUM-A-CHANGE-LANDS-IN-MAINLINE-FIRST: A change lands in mainline *first*; the fan-out is what puts it on the hosts. A web-UI merge is an inbox event, not integration.
facts.SUM-DRIFT-IS-RECONCILED-INTO-MAINLINE: Drift is investigated and reconciled *into* mainline, then re-fanned — never cleared by clobbering the host.
facts.SUM-ONBOARD-AND-OFFBOARD: Onboard a host: empty repo → one manifest entry → first fan-out. Offboard: remove the entry, optionally archive the copy.
facts.SUM-EVERY-HOST-HOLDS-THE-FULL-HISTORY: Every host holds the full history of the refs the manifest declares for it (`main` + tags today; any deliberately declared branch later), so the set grows and shrinks without data loss. Refs outside that set live only where they were authored — the fan-out is replication of a declared line, not a backup of the whole tree.
